findings.title: Remark on [Sta26, Lemma 5] says the bound 236 depends on Stadlmann's Lemma 5, contradicting the paper's own route to 236 through Song--Yue Thm 4.18
findings.location: Remark rem:sta-lemma5, main.tex:1607-1609; also status-table footnote dagger, main.tex:115
findings.quote: \emph{bounds} $240$ and $236$ depend on this input.
findings.claim: Both the 240 and the 236 bound depend on the possibly defective step in the proof of [Sta26, Lemma 5].
findings.analysis: Corollary cor:236 (main.tex:1512-1520) routes the project's 236 exclusively through Song--Yue: ``$H_1\le236$ then follows from \cite[Theorem~4.33]{SY26} and their equidistribution theorem \cite[Theorem~4.18]{SY26}''. The repository's reading notes say Theorem 4.18 is SY's own new estimate, ``proved via IIa, IIb and Type III estimates and a Heath--Brown decomposition (\S\S4.2--4.7)'' (notes/sources-236-song-yue.md:9), and the 14 Nov audit records that ``Nothing of that kind occurs in Song--Yue's own proof (auditors A, B, C). The Siegel--Walfisz factor is always in the slot that needs it'' (notes/audit-sy236-thm418/README.md, Swapped-factor issue). Only Kintali's route (``The analytic input is Stadlmann's (his Prop.~3, with the Type~IIc range made empty)'', main.tex:1385-1386) could pass through Lemma 5, and the paper does not trace whether it does. The sentence therefore attributes to the project's 236 a dependency that its own stated route does not have, and is inconsistent with the 0.2 revision of the companion verification note, which replaced the same sentence by a discussion of which 236 argument may be affected (papers/verification-note/main.tex:480-491). The fact that the dagger footnote (for 240) also carries the sentence ``Both $236$ preprints use the same support'' adds to the confusion about which input belongs to which bound.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the last sentence of rem:sta-lemma5 by: ``The bound $240$ depends on this step. Kintali's route to $236$ uses \cite[Prop.~3]{Sta26} and may depend on it (not traced); Song--Yue's Theorem~4.18, on which Corollary~\ref{cor:236} rests, is proved by their own estimates \cite[\S\S4.2--4.7]{SY26}.'' Move the sentence about the D182 support from the dagger footnote to the double-dagger footnote.

findings.title: The conditional bounds 240 and 236 are described as conditional only on equidistribution estimates; the sieve reductions (Sta26 Prop. 1; SY26 Thm 4.33/sections 4.12-4.14) are also unverified
findings.location: Section 1, main.tex:141-145; abstract main.tex:63-65; Corollaries cor:240 (main.tex:1139-1141) and cor:236 (main.tex:1517-1520); status.json bounds.project_note

findings.claim: The project's 236 (resp. 240) is conditional on the equidistribution theorem of SY26 (resp. the equidistribution estimates of Sta26), and on nothing else.
findings.analysis: Section 1 says 240 is reproduced ``conditionally on the equidistribution estimates of \cite{Sta26}'' and 236 ``conditionally on the equidistribution theorem of \cite{SY26}''; status.json says 236 ``rests on the equidistribution theorem of Song-Yue (... Theorem 4.18, used through their Theorem 4.33)''. But the corollaries themselves need more: cor:240 needs ``his Prop.~1 and his equidistribution theorem'' and cor:236 needs ``\cite[Theorem~4.33]{SY26} and their equidistribution theorem''. Prop.~1 of Sta26 and Thm 4.33 / Prop. 4.21 of SY26 (the derivation of the criterion $48J/I_0>2001/2000$ from the sieve, including the Selberg main term) are claims in unrefereed preprints that the project has not checked; only the numerical inequality was recomputed. The 14 Nov audit lists exactly these as remaining obligations: ``\S4.12 (the reduction to the variational criterion); the Selberg main term ([D14b, Lemma 4.1]); Lemma 4.32'' (notes/audit-sy236-thm418/README.md, What remains). STATE.md item 00 asks the next run to integrate that audit into the status table, cor:236 and status.json; if Theorem 4.18 is then relabelled ``Literature, audited'' while the caveat still names only Theorem 4.18, the remaining unverified reduction would silently disappear from the headline. Also, the relative clause ``which we have not verified'' in cor:236 is ambiguous between Thm 4.18 alone and both theorems.
findings.evidence: main.tex:141-145, 1135-1141, 1512-1520; status.json bounds.project_note; notes/audit-sy236-thm418/README.md; STATE.md Next steps item 00
findings.suggested_fix: Name the full conditional input wherever the conditional bounds appear: for 240, ``conditional on \cite[Prop.~1]{Sta26} and the equidistribution estimates of \cite{Sta26}''; for 236, ``conditional on \cite[Thm.~4.18]{SY26} and on the reduction \cite[\S\S4.12--4.14, Thm.~4.33]{SY26} from it to the variational criterion''. In cor:236 write ``both of which we have not verified''. When the audit is integrated, keep the reduction explicitly listed as unverified.

findings.title: Programme (and status.json) conclude that the 212 draft's value "must belong" to its Table 3 caps, stronger than the body, and the 3.99 ceiling is stated without its single-program/probabilistic basis
findings.location: Programme item 1, main.tex:1739-1741; Prop. prop:cha-ceiling statement main.tex:1302-1311 and discussion main.tex:1334-1342, 1353-1359; abstract main.tex:51-54; status.json results entry for the Lemma 9.1 ceiling
findings.quote: so the draft's value must belong to its Table~3 caps.
findings.claim: The ceiling for the Lemma 9.1 caps proves that the draft value 4.00438 belongs to the Table 3 caps.
findings.analysis: The body is explicitly weaker: ``this suggests that the caps of Lemma~9.1 cannot give their $4.00438$ in a space of this size ... We have not checked that their space is the same as ours (only the dimension is equal), so this is a located discrepancy for the authors or an expert reader, not a refutation'' (main.tex:1353-1359). The Programme and status.json (``So the draft's claimed 4.00438 (also 846 coefficients) must belong to its Table 3 caps'') drop both qualifications. Further, Prop. prop:cha-ceiling is stated unconditionally (``$<3.99<4$ for every $0\ne P\in V$'') and labelled only ``Computed, ball arithmetic'', but its discussion says it ``rests on \texttt{capped\_check.py} ... up to a failure probability below $2^{-31}$ for each functional'' and that ``the cross-check of \texttt{capped\_check.py} itself at these caps is still to come'' (main.tex:1335-1342): unlike every other capped result in the paper, it is a one-program result, and its weights are validated by a randomised identity test. The abstract (``a ceiling certified in ball arithmetic, with weights checked exactly at a random point'') mentions the random point but not the single-program status. The companion verification note made the same correction in its v0.2 (``with a conjecture about the drafting of \cite{Cha26} removed'', papers/verification-note/main.tex changelog).
findings.evidence: main.tex:1302-1359, 1739-1741, 51-54; status.json (Lemma 9.1 ceiling entry); papers/verification-note/main.tex Changes 0.2
findings.suggested_fix: In Programme item 1 replace ``so the draft's value must belong to its Table~3 caps'' by ``which suggests (if their space equals ours) that the draft's value belongs to its Table~3 caps''; make the same change in status.json. Add to the label of prop:cha-ceiling ``one evaluator (\texttt{capped\_check.py}); weights validated by a Schwartz--Zippel test, failure probability $<2^{-31}$'', and say ``one program'' in the abstract.

findings.title: Abstract claims numerical evidence that the k<=29 floor is close to the limit of all (t_m,S)-weights; the paper draws no conclusion in the relevant regime
findings.location: Abstract main.tex:39-42; Prop. prop:family main.tex:798-816 and discussion main.tex:818-827
findings.quote: itself, reach any $k\le29$; numerical evidence that this upper bound is close
findings.claim: There is numerical evidence that the upper bound of Thm floor is close to the limit of every dual weight depending only on t_m and S.
findings.analysis: ``This upper bound'' refers to the bound that excludes $k\le29$. The only regime of prop:family that bears on it is $(k,\varepsilon)=(30,1/4)$, and there the paper says: ``At $(30,1/4)$ the discretisation has not converged (the values still fall, and lie above the continuum value $\le4.0021$ that Theorem~\ref{thm:floor} already certifies), so we draw no conclusion about the exact floor of $\mathcal W$; runs at $k=31,32$ gave $B_{120}=4.0261$ to $4.0976$, also unconverged'' (main.tex:822-826). Evidence of closeness exists only at $(50,1/25)$ ($B_{160}=4.1418$ against $4.1458$), a point where the two-zone weight is not what yields the floor theorem. In addition, prop:family is set as a Proposition although its own label says ``floating point, discretised; not a rigorous bound'', and its text calls the floating-point solver ``an exact convex solver'' (main.tex:804).
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the abstract clause as ``numerical evidence that, at $(k,\varepsilon)=(50,1/25)$, no dual weight depending only on $t_m$ and $t_1+\dots+t_k$ does much better than ours''. Turn prop:family into a Remark (or an ``Observation''), and replace ``an exact convex solver'' by ``a floating-point convex solver''.

findings.location: Section 2.2 after Corollary cor:578, main.tex:341-343; Section 2.4, main.tex:347-348

findings.title: Label system is not applied as defined: "Literature" on statements from unrefereed 2026 preprints, "Computed" on floating-point output, unlabelled results
findings.location: Abstract main.tex:69-72; Section 5 main.tex:886, 1175, 1377, 1393; Remarks/Props with floating-point Computed main.tex:758, 798, 832, 1161-1163; unlabelled Corollaries cor:578, cor:246 (main.tex:330, 418), Remarks at main.tex:732, 770, 1361, 1711; README.md Labels section
findings.quote: directions that later versions will test. Every statement carries one of the
findings.claim: Every statement carries exactly one of the six labels, and the labels mean what the abstract and README say.
findings.analysis: (a) The abstract defines \lbl{Claimed} as ``a preprint not yet independently verified'', yet statements read from those preprints are labelled \lbl{Literature}: ``The following is \lbl{Literature}, read in \cite[Def.~1, Def.~5, Prop.~1]{Sta26}'' (main.tex:886) covers Stadlmann's criterion, i.e. the claimed implication criterion $\Rightarrow\DHL$; likewise Kintali's support (main.tex:1377), SY's criterion (main.tex:1393, 1442) and the Charton caps (main.tex:1175). The label then conflates refereed results (Maynard, Polymath8b) with transcriptions from preprints. (b) README.md defines ``\textbf{Computed} (exact certificate)'' and the paper's ``Rules'' require an exact certificate for the project column, but \lbl{Computed} is also attached to floating-point, discretised or sampled output (``\lbl{Computed}, floating point only'' main.tex:758; prop:family main.tex:798; Collatz--Wielandt sampling main.tex:832; Remark rem:k49's extrapolation draws on Computed values). (c) Several results carry no label (Corollaries cor:578 and cor:246, which are the end-to-end reproductions; Remarks at main.tex:732, 770, 1361, 1711), several carry two, and new ad hoc labels appear (``\lbl{Literature} reading, not a result'', main.tex:1594). The label system is the paper's main device for calibrating claims, so its inconsistent use weakens the calibration it is meant to provide.
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce two sub-labels and use them throughout: \lbl{Claimed} for every statement (definition, criterion, estimate) taken from an unrefereed preprint, keeping \lbl{Literature} for refereed sources; and \lbl{Computed (exact)} versus \lbl{Numerical} (floating point, not a bound). Label the two end-to-end corollaries (e.g. ``\lbl{Computed} + \lbl{Lean-checked} + \lbl{Literature} inputs''). Align the README definition with the paper.

findings.title: Proposition prop:adjoint is labelled "Proved here" but is a description of program internals with no proof
findings.location: Proposition prop:adjoint, main.tex:1250-1264
findings.quote: \begin{proposition}[\lbl{Proved here}; elementary]\label{prop:adjoint}
findings.claim: The reverse-mode Gram construction is a proved mathematical statement.
findings.analysis: The statement begins ``In the direct method of \texttt{code/capped\_check.py}, $I_T$ is a linear function of the coefficient products ...'' and its objects ($\kappa_I$, $w_I$, ``the chain of exact linear maps of that program'', $Q$ ``the (sparse, explicit) map'') are defined only by reference to code. No proof follows (the next text is a sloppypar about running time and a self-test). What is actually established is an implementation property, checked by an exact self-test at three inputs and by a Schwartz--Zippel identity test at one random point. Labelling it \lbl{Proved here} places it in the same evidence class as the paper's genuine propositions (rigid, exact, bonf).
findings.suggested_fix: Relabel as a description of method (e.g. a Remark ``Gram matrices by reverse mode'', \lbl{Computed}: validated by the exact self-tests), or state the underlying mathematical fact (``$I_T(P1_T)$ is a quadratic form in the coefficients whose matrix entries depend only on $F_1+F_2$ and $a_1+a_2$'') and prove that.

findings.title: "Lean-checked" attached to real-coordinate geometric facts that Lean proves only for natural-number coordinates
findings.location: Remark rem:ceiling main.tex:1157-1158; proof of Prop. prop:exact main.tex:1074-1075; main.tex:1177-1180, 1383-1385; lean/TwinPrimes/Caps.lean
findings.quote: Every coordinate of a point of $T$ is at most $0.6$
findings.claim: Facts about all real points of the supports (coordinate bound 0.6, at most 9/16/10 large coordinates, j<=3/6) are kernel-checked.
findings.analysis: Caps.lean states each lemma for lists of natural numbers in units of 1/1000, 1/1250 or 1/2500, e.g. \texttt{theorem stadlmann\_coord\_le (x : Nat) (l : List Nat) (h : ∀ y ∈ l, 112 < y) ...}. For real coordinates (which are not multiples of the unit) these lemmas do not formally imply the stated facts; the transfer uses a further, unchecked, rounding argument (here trivial, but it is the step that the label claims was checked). The facts are true, so there is no mathematical consequence; the issue is the calibration of the label that the paper uses as its strongest evidence class.
findings.suggested_fix: Write ``(the integer-unit version is \lbl{Lean-checked}: ...; the real case follows by the same linear inequality)'' or restate the lemmas over $\mathbb Q$ in Lean.

findings.title: Title "Toward the twin prime conjecture" frames the work as progress toward H_1=2, which Section 1 says it cannot be
findings.location: Title, main.tex:21; Section 1, main.tex:147-152
findings.quote: \title[Toward the twin prime conjecture]{Toward the twin prime conjecture: certificates, limits of the sieve, and a working programme}
findings.claim: The paper is a contribution toward the twin prime conjecture.
findings.analysis: Every result concerns $H_1\ge236$ or limits of sieve supports; Section 1 states ``No amount of success on Track~A reaches $2$'' (main.tex:152), and Track B contains only a reading list and an informal problem (main.tex:1777-1793). findings.title: I, J name the capped functionals (t-scale), the cap-free functionals (u-scale) and SY's capped numerator in successive paragraphs; I_0/J_0 and I(P)/J(P) are two names for the cap-free ones
findings.quote: write $I(P)$, $J(P)$ for the cap-free
findings.claim: The symbols I, J, I_T, J_T, I_0, J_0 have fixed meanings.
findings.analysis: (1) main.tex:894-897: ``the functional $J(F)$ of \cite{Sta26} is the integral of $(\int F\,dt_k)^2$ over $t_1+\dots+t_{k-1}\le A_1-\varepsilon$ ..., $I(F)=\int_{T_k}F^2$'': capped, Stadlmann scale, threshold 1. (2) main.tex:942: ``write $I(P)$, $J(P)$ for the cap-free functionals on $L\R_k$'': cap-free, Polymath scale. (3) main.tex:1440: ``$I_0$ is the \emph{cap-free} mass on $\{s<U\}$, $J$ the capped numerator'', and the criterion ``$48J/I_0>\frac{2001}{2000}$'' (also in the abstract, main.tex:62, and in cor:236) uses $J$ for the capped numerator, while two pages later ``$\mathrm{Corr}_1/J=2.3\cdot10^{-6}$'' (main.tex:1500) uses $J$ for the cap-free one, and $J_0$ is introduced as a third name for it. Theorem thm:hybrid-floor uses meaning (1) in its hypothesis and the Polymath-scale $M_k(\cdot,\cdot)>4$ in its conclusion. A reader cannot tell from the symbol whether a ratio is capped or cap-free, or at which threshold (1, $2001/2000$ or 4) it is to be compared.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix once (in the subsection ``The support and the criterion''): $I_0(P),J_0(P)$ cap-free, $I_T,J_T$ capped, all in the $u$-scale with threshold 4; write Stadlmann's and Song--Yue's functionals as $I^{\mathrm{St}},J^{\mathrm{St}}$ (threshold 1) only when quoting them, and write the SY criterion as $48J_T/I_0>4\cdot\frac{2001}{2000}$ in $u$-scale. Replace $\mathrm{Corr}_1/J$ by $\mathrm{Corr}_1/J_0$.

findings.title: Scale of coordinates t vs u=4t drifts: T is defined in t-coordinates but used as a subset of u-space; one display gives the same ratio 48J_T/I_0 in two scalings
findings.location: Definition of T main.tex:889-893; Prop. prop:exact(1) main.tex:1030; Remark rem:ceiling main.tex:1157; Prop. prop:sy-exact(3) main.tex:1461-1464; Prop. prop:adjoint main.tex:1260
findings.claim: Coordinates and ratios are in the declared Polymath scaling u=4t.
findings.analysis: $T_k$ is ``the set of $t\in[0,1]^k$ such that ... $\sum_{i\in I}t_i\le B_{j,|I|}$'' (main.tex:889-892), with caps $B\approx0.15$. After ``In the Polymath scaling $u=4t$'' (main.tex:906), the paper keeps writing $T$ for the scaled set: ``the fiber $\{t\ge0:(u',t)\in T\}$'' with $t$ compared with $g=4\delta$ (main.tex:1030, 1052), and ``Every coordinate of a point of $T$ is at most $0.6$'' (main.tex:1157), which is false for $T$ as defined (coordinates $\le0.15$) and true for $4T$. Here $t$ is also the $u$-scale last coordinate, two lines after $u=4t$ was declared. In prop:sy-exact(3), ``$48J_T/I_0=1.000664921591\ldots$ ... i.e.\ $4.0026596864\ldots$ in our scaling'' gives two values to one expression, then ``$48J_T/I_T=4.0030988047\ldots$'' is in the other scale; since $kJ/I$ is not scale-invariant (it is multiplied by 4 under $u=4t$), the symbols do not determine the number. In prop:adjoint, $t_1,t_2$ denote basis polynomials (``for basis terms $t_i=(L-P_1)^{a_i}\prod_jP_j^{F_{i,j}}$'').
findings.suggested_fix: Write $T^{u}=4T$ (or redefine $T$ in $u$-coordinates once, with caps $C_m$ and threshold $g$) and use $x$ or $u_k$ for the last coordinate of a fiber. In prop:sy-exact(3) state one scaling and give the other in words (``$1.000664921591$ in Song--Yue's normalisation''). Rename the basis terms in prop:adjoint (e.g. $\beta_1,\beta_2$).

findings.title: U, s, V, P, R, F, M, sigma each carry two or three live meanings inside Section 5
findings.location: Section 5 (main.tex:876-1723), with cross-section clashes in Sections 3-4
findings.quote: $U=\min\left(R,\max(g,\,C_{m(u')+1}-s(u'))\right)$;
findings.claim: Symbols have one meaning within a section.
findings.analysis: $U$: fiber endpoint $U(u')$ (main.tex:1032; used in $Q(u',U)$, Corr$_2$, prop:bonf and main.tex:1590) vs. Song--Yue's scalar $U=\frac{521}{2000}$ (main.tex:1437, already used undefined in the dilation $z=\frac{26}{25U}t$ at main.tex:1389). $s$: scale factor $s=(L+\tau)/2=4A_1$ (main.tex:909; ``$s\,kJ/I=4.01618$'', main.tex:1005) vs. large-set sum $s(u)=\sum_{i\in I(u)}u_i$ (main.tex:1022; $r_A=s-mg$, $\rho=|u|-s-jg$) vs. the full coordinate sum $s(z)$ in ``$(\frac{26}{25}-s(z))^a$'' (main.tex:1435, 1448, since $\frac{26}{25}-s(z)=\frac{520}{521}(L-P_1(u))$). $V$: cap-violation set $V=L\R_k\setminus T$ (main.tex:943; $\int_VP^2$ in prop:exact and prop:bonf) vs. ``let $V$ be our $846$-dimensional space'' (main.tex:1305, ``$0\ne P\in V$''). $P$: test polynomial vs. power sums $P_j$ vs. working precision ``$P=5000$ bits'' (main.tex:1317) vs. the polytope $P$ in prop:rigid (main.tex:483). $R$: fiber length $R=L-|u'|$ vs. the regions $R_m(g,c)$ vs. the simplex $\R_k$. $F$: test function vs. exponent multi-index in prop:adjoint ($\kappa_I[F]$, $F_1+F_2=F$). $M$: $M_k$ vs. the coefficient bound $M:=\sum_i|c_i|L^{a_i+w(b_i)}$ (main.tex:1579). $\sigma$: $1-\sum u$ (prop:rigid), $|t'|$ (thm:floor), the ceiling level in $\sigma G_I-kG_J$ (main.tex:1275), and the undefined shell variable ``$\rho<\sigma\le1$'' (main.tex:668-669) where the proof used $S$. The clashes of $U$, $s$ and $V$ are within a few pages of each other and inside formulas that the reader must evaluate.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename: $U_{\mathrm{SY}}$ for $\frac{521}{2000}$ (as the verification note v0.2 did), $\lambda$ for the scale factor $4A_1$, $s_A(u)$ for the large-set sum and $|z|$ for the total, $\mathcal V_{21}$ for the test space, ``$p$ bits'' for the precision, $\alpha$ for exponent vectors in prop:adjoint, $M_c$ for the coefficient bound, and replace $\sigma$ by $S$ at main.tex:668.

findings.title: The abstract is a single 45-line sentence mixing a dozen results, reproductions, caveats and version history
findings.location: Abstract, main.tex:28-73
findings.quote: function of degree~$22$ gives $4.0061>4$ (two independent exact programs since version~0.12), and
findings.claim: The abstract tells the reader what the paper delivers.
findings.analysis: Item (iii) of the abstract runs from main.tex:35 to main.tex:67 as one clause list joined by semicolons, containing four version references (``since version~0.12'', ``since version~0.11'', ``version~0.12 adds''), numerical values to four or five decimals, file-level detail (``exact Gram matrices obtained by running the exact evaluator backwards'', ``with weights checked exactly at a random point''), and three different caveats. It also mixes the project's own results (rigidity, EGF formula, floors, Bonferroni) with reproductions of others' variational steps under the heading ``small results of our own''. An expert cannot see from it which statements are the paper's contributions, which are reproductions, and which caveat attaches to which number. There are also attribution slips (``raises his margin only from $4.0120$ to $4.0124$'', main.tex:56: both values are for the project's test functions, not Stadlmann's).
findings.suggested_fix: Restructure as 5-7 sentences: (1) scope and the explicit non-claims; (2) three numbers (246 established; 182 claimed; 236/240 reproduced conditionally, naming the unverified inputs); (3) reproductions: exact variational steps for 240, 236 (published witness and own $F$), 212 with Table~3 caps, plus the Lemma~9.1 ceiling; (4) own results: Prop.~\ref{prop:rigid}/\ref{prop:rigid-eps}, Lemma~\ref{lem:egf}, Theorems~\ref{thm:floor} and \ref{thm:hybrid-floor}, Prop.~\ref{prop:bonf}; (5) labels. Move version information to a changelog.

findings.title: Version history and process narration inside the mathematics; superseded results kept as numbered propositions; a section title that is out of date
findings.location: Section 5 title main.tex:876; subsection headings main.tex:788, 1017, 1169, 1244, 1375, 1433, 1528; Prop. prop:capped and text main.tex:988-1015; main.tex:115, 133-135, 742-744, 783-785, 881-883, 1208, 1361-1373, 1486-1491
findings.quote: \section{Stadlmann-type supports (versions 0.5--0.9)}\label{sec:stad}
findings.claim: The paper is organised by mathematics.
findings.analysis: Section 5 is titled ``(versions 0.5--0.9)'' but contains v0.10--v0.12 material (Song--Yue, the second program, Bonferroni); its subsections are titled by version (``(version 0.6)'', ``(version 0.7)'', ``(version 0.8)'', ``(versions 0.8--0.9)'', ``(version 0.10)'', ``(version 0.12)''), and so is a subsection of Section 4 (``(version 0.4)''). Prop.~\ref{prop:capped} (3.95972) is kept as a numbered proposition although the text says ``Theorem~\ref{thm:capped-exact} below supersedes it'' (main.tex:999); the next paragraph explains a failed attempt (``$E/I\approx146$''). Throughout there is lab-notebook detail: which helper read which source, ``on 12 November the file was too large for our reader and direct download was refused'' (main.tex:134-135), ``An earlier draft of this remark, version~0.3 as first circulated'' (main.tex:783-784), minutes and cores for every run, checkpoint resumption. For an expert reader this obscures which statement is current and which is history; the theorem-numbered superseded result is the most costly instance.
findings.suggested_fix: Title sections by content (``Exact capped functionals and the 2026 one-band supports''); drop version tags from headings and theorem labels; demote Prop.~\ref{prop:capped} to one sentence in a remark (``a Cauchy--Schwarz bound gives only $3.9597$''); move provenance (helpers, run times, resumed runs) to a Reproducibility appendix and the version narrative to a changelog at the end, as the verification note does.

findings.title: Main own results are hard to find: the hybrid floor and the Bonferroni proposition are buried at the end of a half-paper Section 5 that interleaves four claimed bounds
findings.location: Section 5, main.tex:876-1723 (about 850 of 1850 lines); Thm thm:hybrid-floor main.tex:1658-1709; Prop. prop:bonf main.tex:1528-1592; Remark rem:oai186 main.tex:1612-1656
findings.quote: \subsection*{A floor for one-band hybrid supports (our own)}
findings.claim: A reader can find the main results.
findings.analysis: The Programme calls the floor problem ``our main original direction'' (main.tex:1751), but its main theorem for the 2026 supports, Theorem~\ref{thm:hybrid-floor}, appears at the very end of Section 5, after the 186 reading remark and long computational subsections, although it uses only Section 4 (Lemma~\ref{lem:dual}, Theorem~\ref{thm:floor}, eq.~\eqref{eq:dil}) and nothing from the capped computations. Section 5 interleaves the method (prop:caps, prop:exact, prop:adjoint, prop:bonf), four different targets (240, 212, 236 twice) and a literature remark on 186. The headings ``Results of our own'' for Sections 3--4 suggest that Section 5 contains no own results, which is false (prop:exact, prop:adjoint, prop:bonf, thm:hybrid-floor, rem:ceiling). There is no single list or table of what is reproduced for which bound with which evidence (the verification note has one).
findings.suggested_fix: Move Theorem~\ref{thm:hybrid-floor} and its remark to the end of Section~4 (as ``one-band hybrid supports''); split Section~5 into ``Exact capped functionals'' (support, prop:exact, the two evaluators, prop:adjoint, prop:bonf) and ``Application to the claimed bounds 240, 236, 212'' with a summary table (bound, $k$, test function, value, programs, unverified input); move rem:oai186 and rem:sta-lemma5 to a short section on the analytic inputs.

findings.title: Redundancy, and a Programme section that is mostly status recap and a reading list; the Track B problem is not well posed
findings.location: Programme main.tex:1725-1798; status-table footnote main.tex:115 vs Remark rem:sta-lemma5 main.tex:1594-1610; duplicate definitions of M_{k,eps} main.tex:363-371 and 514-524
findings.quote: \item \emph{Climb the ladder.} The certified pipeline now stands at $k=50$
findings.claim: The Programme states the research directions.
findings.analysis: Track A item 1 (main.tex:1729-1750) restates Section 5 result by result with version numbers (``version~0.6 reproduces'', ``version~0.7 confirms'', ``version~0.8 has the tool'', ``(version~0.12)''); it opens with ``The certified pipeline now stands at $k=50$'' although the same item then reports $k=49$ and $k=48$. The 236 status appears in the abstract, Section 1, two footnotes, two subsections of Section 5, cor:236 and here. The dagger footnote of the status table (main.tex:115) repeats Remark rem:sta-lemma5 almost verbatim. $M_{k,\varepsilon}$ and the validity conditions of its criterion are defined twice (main.tex:363-371 and 514-524). Track B announces ``We will study, one per session, what each would need'' (main.tex:1780-1781): a work plan, not mathematics. The second Problem asks for ``the weakest known input that implies the twin prime conjecture'' (main.tex:1790-1791), which has no definite meaning (``weakest'' in what order? ``known'' to whom?), so it cannot be answered or checked.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut Track A item 1 to one sentence pointing to the summary table proposed in P5-E03; keep in the Programme only open problems stated precisely (the Problem after Track A is a good model); shorten the dagger footnote to one line referring to rem:sta-lemma5; define $M_{k,\varepsilon}$ once; replace the Track B problem by a precise statement (e.g. ``formalise Heath-Brown's implication: infinitely many exceptional characters $\Rightarrow$ twin primes, with the hypothesis stated explicitly'') or drop it.
